title: Fan stitch
subtitle: Seven or more trebles from a single chain space, opening into a wide arc
excerpt: The fan stitch places seven (or more) trebles into a single chain space, spreading them into a wide arc. The result is more dramatic than the shell: the fan covers more space, the arc is deeper, and the fabric reads as decorative from across the room.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 4 and 5 (Internet Archive). Fan stitch and large-shell variations in traditional Victorian and Edwardian crochet.
heroPrompt: A swatch of fan stitch in cream DK cotton, showing wide fan-shaped groups of trebles fanning across the fabric, natural linen background, close up showing the arc shape.

glossaryTerms.definition: Seven or more trebles worked into a single chain space, spreading into a wide arc. A large-scale version of the shell stitch. The deep arc distinguishes the fan from the more compact five-treble shell.

content.text: extends the shell principle to seven or more trebles. Where a five-treble shell fits neatly above a single stitch, a seven-treble fan works across a chain space so the base has room for the spreading arc. The effect is more architectural: a pronounced sweep that casts a visible shadow at the base.
Work to the chain space that is the fan's base (typically a ch-3 or ch-4 space that gives the fan room to spread).
Work 7 complete trebles, all into the same chain space. Each treble is worked normally.
The seven trebles fan out above the chain space, spreading from a narrow base to a wide arc at the top.
Row 1: ch 1, dc in 2nd ch from hook, *ch 3, skip 4 ch, dc in next ch; repeat from * across. Turn.
Row 2 (fan row): ch 1, dc in first dc, *7tr fan into ch-3 space, dc in next dc; repeat from * across. Turn.
Row 3: ch 4, *dc into centre (4th) tr of fan, ch 3; repeat from * across, dc at end. Turn.

items.symptom: The fan does not lie flat — the outer trebles bunch up
items.cause: The chain space base is too small for seven trebles.
items.fix: Use a ch-4 or ch-5 base space. If the pattern uses ch-3, try working the outer trebles at a slightly looser tension so they can spread.

items.symptom: The return-row dc is hard to find at the centre of the fan
items.cause: The centre treble is not easy to identify among seven.
items.fix: Count: for a 7-tr fan, the centre is position 4. Mark it with a stitch marker on the first few rows.

content.text: The fan works in double trebles instead of trebles for an even more dramatic arc — often seen in shawl patterns. The crossed treble stitch uses a similar wide-fan principle but with the legs crossing each other, creating a different texture at the same scale.
